prompts.prompt: Audit shared/skills/research for team-use readiness. Do not edit the target Skill; choose alignment, report, and summary artifact paths automatically; validate confirmed alignment before any formal verdict; include capability_baseline_ref, confirmed_target_capability_ids, confirmed_gap_refs, and evidence_checks for every P0/P1 finding; write a Markdown summary with per-finding evidence, impact, repair target, and verification hint; run both validators; and return a formal verdict in the same run only after confirmation.

Do a quick, non-final light scan of shared/skills/research for likely readiness issues. Return only unranked candidate risks; do not issue severity labels, readiness verdicts, report-path requests, or ask for a second request.

Review whether shared/skills/skill-quality-audit/evals/fixtures/artifacts/overview-transcript.md is a valid skill-quality-audit result. Classify the artifact first; if it is a transcript, reject it as a report and treat its claims only as leads for a fresh formal audit.

A user asks for a normal code review of tests/test-skill-quality-audit-runtime-contract.sh, not for a Skill readiness audit. Explain that skill-quality-audit should stay inactive and route to ordinary code review.

Validate a skill-quality-audit alignment artifact that is still awaiting user confirmation but already includes a readiness verdict or severity finding. Reject it before any formal report validator claim.
Validate a skill-quality-audit JSON report fixture whose P1 evidence_checks expected_snippet no longer appears at the cited path:line. Reject the readiness claim through the validator path.
Given a validator-passing skill-quality-audit report, extract only the repair targets, owner handoff, and verification commands needed by a separate implementation window. Do not replay the audit.
Audit whether a retired Skill name still appears in active runtime, install, gate, test, eval, or downstream consumer paths. Do not modify files.
Review a Skill line by line for vague instructions, broad objects, hidden conditions, and missing failure handling. Return a 10-point Instruction Contract score.
